subject: Emergency telemetry safeguard hotfix — actions for impacted deployments
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: alice.park@acme-analytics.com, ops-team@acme-analytics.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 16:15:00 -0800
Subject: Emergency telemetry safeguard hotfix — actions for impacted deployments

Hi Alice / Acme Ops,

We just discovered a telemetry exporter edge-case that, under certain high-cardinality usage patterns, can cause brief event-loop stalls inside the inference worker process. For hosted customers we rolled a short, targeted safeguard today that reduces exporter batching and enables sampling to avoid backpressure; for Dedicated/Private deployments we are shipping the minimal hotfix attached.

Impact (what we saw):
- Intermittent ~100–300ms tail latency spikes for token generation during telemetry flushes.
- No inference decisions or model weights were modified; no persisted customer data was lost.

Immediate actions we recommend (pick what applies):
1) Hosted customers: no action required; the safeguard is live for the hosted fleet and we are monitoring.
2) Dedicated / Private: apply the attached hotfix (telemetry_hotfix_v1.patch) to your inference runtime and restart the inference service. If you cannot restart immediately, set the runtime env var REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_SAMPLING=0.1 to reduce exporter throughput until you can apply the patch.

Attachments included: telemetry_hotfix_v1.patch (patch), telemetry_hotfix_release_notes.pdf (one-pager).

Expected next steps from us:
- We will follow up with verification metrics and a postmortem draft within 48 hours.
- If you see increased latency after applying the patch, please reply with a short support bundle (time window, request ids).

We appreciate the quick notice this causes — I will keep you updated as we validate the rollout.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Emergency telemetry safeguard hotfix — actions for impacted deployments

Team — quick context and plan: 

Root cause (initial): the Prometheus/metrics-exporter client we forked for high-throughput traces was doing synchronous disk buffering on path X when cardinality exceeded our internal sampling threshold. Under high cardinality that hit a synchronized flush and introduced event-loop stalls (seen in p95+ goroutine pauses).

What we pushed (hosted):
- Flip telemetry sampler to probabilistic mode (0.1) + reduce exporter buffer size. This is intentionally conservative and will reduce metrics fidelity but eliminates exporter-induced stalls.

Customer-facing plan (Dedicated/Private):
- Ship telemetry_hotfix_v1.patch (attached) — minimal code change to make exporter flush asynchronous.
- Provide a CLI env toggle (REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_SAMPLING) to customers for immediate mitigation.
- If any customer reports regression after patch, execute rollback plan: restore exporter to previous sync path and revert sampling change; mark as priority and escalate to infra-on-call.

Marissa — can you coordinate slice of customers that need manual outreach (I started with Acme)? Rishi — please prepare a short verification dashboard and share link. Jonas — schedule a postmortem slot for 11/05 10:00 PST and add the impacted customers as optional attendees.

Neha

Subject: Re: Emergency telemetry safeguard hotfix — actions for impacted deployments

Hi Alice — thanks for the quick reply and for the log snippet. Short answers: 

- The patch requires a graceful restart of the inference worker process; a rolling restart of worker pods is sufficient (no database migrations or model reloads). Expected disruption: a handful of requests might move to warm-up latency for a moment, but no inference failures expected.
- Setting REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_SAMPLING=0.1 is safe from a correctness perspective — it only affects telemetry emission, not inference outputs. SDK integrations are unaffected; only the metrics payload is sampled.

We applied the patch to the hosted fleet at 02:45 UTC and validated p99 latency dropped back to baseline for impacted fleets. I attached a short verification link with the relevant Grafana view (postdeploy-verification-grafana-link.txt).

Next: if you are able to apply the patch tonight, please restart workers in a rolling fashion. If you prefer, we can coordinate a hands-on window and a Redwood engineer (I can have Rishi or Jonas join).

We will share a postmortem draft and invite you to the 11/05 10:00 PST postmortem where we will walk the cause, timelines, and longer-term fixes (improved exporter resiliency + stronger e2e latency alerts).

Attachments: telemetry_hotfix_v1.patch (patch), telemetry_hotfix_release_notes.pdf (pdf), postdeploy-verification-grafana-link.txt (text)
